parsed.explanation: The combined regime pairs a hostile federal layer with a hostile state layer. Universal exposures: visa/entry screening where document or 'reasonable doubt' about sex triggers refusal and possible lifetime fraud findings; facility exclusion by assigned sex in all public schools and government buildings, enforced by a public complaint form whose documentary defence (state-issued birth certificate/surgery proof) a visitor cannot meet; a documented arrest (trespass, men's-ward holding). Federal custody carries documented conversion-therapy-style policies and abuse. Weighed against: private venues (hotels, gyms) exempt, single-occupant facilities required in new buildings, functioning courts (orders enjoined), state hate-crime statute covering gender identity, employment protection, no sodomy or identity criminalisation. Documented exposures are continuous but rarely custodial; remedies partially work.

entry_documents.exposure: Feb 2025 cable tags visa cases; document discrepancy or 'reasonable doubt' about sex instructs refusal and additional evidence; possible lifetime fraud ineligibility. X markers discontinued; several governments issued travel advisories. Airport screening outing risk documented.
entry_documents.protection: Fraud finding requires all four elements, is never automatic, has limited waiver; suit challenging passport policy pending; several orders enjoined.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry refusal escalates to fraud finding → stranded traveller, then state facility rules govern any stay.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented arrest of a trans woman under the state's bathroom trespass law, held 24 hours in a men's ward (up to 60 days misdemeanour). Federal corrections bureau adopted conversion-therapy-style policies (hair, hormones, psychiatric drugs); immigration custody reports beatings, solitary, sexual abuse of trans detainees.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Complaint-driven enforcement, not police sweeps; trespass requires willful entry plus refusal to leave; constitutional challenge to analogous laws noted.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Document discrepancy or facility complaint can move a visitor into custody where federal/state custody practices apply.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: State bars assigned-sex-incongruent restroom/locker use in all public schools and government buildings, reaching adults; public reporting form invites third-party outing. Parent framework: federal order bars trans people from federally funded single-sex facilities; 4 state/provinces criminalise in some circumstances.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Private businesses (hotels, gyms, commercial venues) explicitly outside the state law; new government buildings must include single-occupant facilities; 29 state/provinces plus capital have no mapped ban.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal funding rules reinforce state bans; visitor's best shelters are private venues.

care_services.exposure: State bans gender-affirming care for minors (visitor's minor would be refused); legislature dismissed a commissioned review upholding the treatments. Federal October 2025 rule would bar public-insurance reimbursement for under-18 care; DOJ subpoenaed hospital records of patients under 19.
care_services.protection: Adult care not restricted in the dossier; clinicians may treat patients under 25; 2015 non-discrimination statute covers employment/housing.
care_services.interaction: Emergency disclosure of trans status can trigger facility and document rules simultaneously.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Executive orders label care 'mutilation', direct law enforcement to investigate 'gender ideology'; counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' groups; flag ban with $500/day fines; advocacy director calls the state the leader in anti-LGBTQ legislation. 66% public support for birth-sex documents.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Reward criteria never use 'gender ideology' as a trigger; strategy states counterterrorism powers won't target mere disagreement; national hate-crime statute covers gender identity.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing raises the probability that complaints under the facility law are pursued.

minors_guardians.exposure: A travelling minor faces the same school/government facility bans; care ban blocks treatment for under-18s; federal order directs criminal investigation of adults facilitating a trans minor's social transition, framed as exploitation or unlicensed practice.
minors_guardians.protection: Care ban reviewed as potentially unconstitutional; constitutional challenges pending; conversion-therapy ban for minors in state (with clergy/parent exemptions).
minors_guardians.interaction: A parent accompanying a trans minor risks being cast as facilitating transition under the Jan 2025 order.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state-specific violence data located. National statistics show sexual-orientation bias at one-seventh to one-fifth of single-bias incidents. State hate-crime statute amended 2019 to cover gender identity with enhanced penalties and mandatory statistics.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Documented state hate-crime statute covering gender identity; national hate-crime law; employment and housing non-discrimination; no sodomy or identity-expression criminalisation.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Thin local violence data leaves street risk genuinely uncertain rather than demonstrated safe.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No complaint data or outcomes under the 2024 facility law; unclear whether the documentary defence works with out-of-state documents; gender-identity-specific hate-crime figures not located; national posture contested and changing.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Functioning courts: orders enjoined, suits pending, legal-aid FAQ maintained; 2019 hate-crime amendments passed near-unanimously; 2021 court held name/sex changes must be granted; marriage equality and employment protection in force.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Recourse exists but is uneven — only 23 state/provinces cover gender identity in bias statutes; 22 plus capital bar identity discrimination.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: routine, unavoidable exposure at checkpoints and in public buildings, lengthy verification, documented detention and denial of care, scarce or contested remedies, inconsistent enforcement. Higher than 0.45-A only in that this dossier adds a documented arrest with opposite-sex ward holding and an official complaint mechanism; lower in that private venues are exempt and federal courts demonstrably enjoin measures.

Lower than 0.55-B. That anchor's harm is administrative secondary screening and refused admission with written appeal; here entry friction can escalate to a lifetime fraud ineligibility finding, and the state layer adds criminal trespass exposure (arrest documented, men's ward) plus a third-party reporting channel. Recourse here is stronger (courts working, hate-crime statute), but severity tiers differ.

Materially lower. 0.75-C features trained, respectful border inspection, brief detention ending in release, compensation for unlawful holding and a tribunal that hears appeals. Here the state documents an actual arrest and custody in a men's ward, plus a universal facility-exclusion rule and hostile federal entry screening — exposures absent from that anchor.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller faces two reinforcing systems: federal entry/document screening engineered to catch sex-document discrepancy (refusal, possible lifetime fraud bar, consular advisories from eight governments), and state facility exclusion by assigned sex in every public school and government building, policed by a public complaint form whose defence requires documents the visitor will not hold. Private accommodation and commerce remain outside the ban, and single-occupant facilities are required in new buildings, so everyday lodging and commerce are comparatively safe. Custody is the sharp edge: one documented arrest with 24 hours in a men's ward, plus federal corrections and immigration-custody practices rated as conversion therapy and abuse. Functioning courts, a gender-identity hate-crime statute and employment protection prevent this reaching the lower tiers, but they have not stopped the operative exposures — placing it firmly in Elevated Risk.
